schemes.official_name: DU Gestion de projet entrepreneurial et intrapreneurial (parcours européen / 4EU+)
schemes.english_name: University Diploma in Entrepreneurial and Intrapreneurial Project Management (European/4EU+ track)
schemes.description: Seven-month university diploma: interdisciplinary European teams of students and doctoral candidates work on a concrete challenge proposed by a partner organisation (company, public institution, NGO, laboratory or association), with academic advisors and professional partners; kick-off bootcamp Nov 2026, final defence before a European jury June 2027. French-language track also exists (2022 article: sponsor ('commanditaire') submits a technological or societal problem to the project team; example Safran aircraft waste reduction).
schemes.admin_host: Faculté des Sciences et Ingénierie (4EU+ version) / CELSA and Pépite Sorbonne Université (French track, per 2022 article)
schemes.eligible_faculties_programmes: Primarily doctoral students at 4EU+ alliance universities; subject to availability Master's students completing M2 by 15 Oct 2026 and recent Master's graduates; no prior entrepreneurship experience needed
schemes.eligibility_restrictions: Bac+5 holders (master/doctorate); mainly doctoral students of 4EU+ universities
schemes.credit_assessment: University diploma (DU, Bac+6 level per 2022 article); assessment by individual and group deliverables, interim presentations, final defence before a European jury. ECTS not found.
schemes.delivery_format: Interdisciplinary team project with bootcamp, coaching, final defence
schemes.project_evidence: Teams design, test and present solutions to a partner-set challenge; prototypes/deliverables and final defence [1].
schemes.group_evidence: 'interdisciplinary European teams composed of students and doctoral candidates' with group deliverables assessed [1].
schemes.employer_evidence: Challenge proposed by a partner organisation (company, public institution, NGO, laboratory or association) [1]; 2022 article: a 'commanditaire' submits the problem to the team [2]. The 4EU+ page lists partner types including laboratories, so the share of commercial vs internal/research partners is not separable.
schemes.partner_role: Proposes challenge; supports teams as professional partner; (French track) commissioner of the project
schemes.named_partners: Safran (2022 French-track project example, 'La réduction des déchets en avion avec Safran'); no 2026/27 partners found
schemes.deliverable: Prototype/solution, deliverables and presentation before European jury
schemes.unresolved: Whether every project has an external organisation (page says challenge 'proposed by a partner organization' but lists laboratories among partner types); named 2026/27 partners; ECTS; the page's 'seven months' vs older sources' 'six months'. Eligibility is largely doctoral/post-master, so not open to ordinary undergraduates. External coverage set to All/standard because the page says each challenge is 'proposed by a partner organization'.

profile_md:
Two routes meet all three criteria with current delivery evidence, and both are narrow in who can join.

**DU Gestion de projet entrepreneurial et intrapreneurial (4EU+ European track)**: interdisciplinary teams of students and doctoral candidates work for seven months (Nov 2026-June 2027) on a challenge proposed by a partner organisation (company, public institution, NGO, laboratory or association), ending in a defence before a European jury. It is aimed primarily at doctoral students of 4EU+ universities and, subject to availability, new master's graduates, so it is not open to ordinary undergraduates. A 2022 article on the French track describes a 'commanditaire' submitting a problem (e.g. Safran aircraft waste reduction).

**Polytech Sorbonne projets industriels**: year 4-5 engineering students in teams of 4-6 with an industrial client and an academic tutor (semester or year, ~100 h per student); the MAIN year-4 curriculum for 2026-2027 lists the module. Whether it is compulsory in every specialty and its ECTS are not stated.

Near-misses: a maths M1 TER with optional industrial question (pairs possible), and an M2 health business-plan unit where the project holders are not shown to be organisations. Pépite/SNEE is entrepreneurship support and is excluded. Sorbonne has no business school; CELSA collective projects have no evidenced external client. Provision is distributed across schools rather than institution-wide. Pages were French; extracts translated and original language noted.
gaps: Reduced-depth pass (~9 searches, plus fetches). Not opened: CELSA RH master 'Projet collectif', Doctorat-Conseil, Lettres masters (Médiation de la musique, Humanités numériques), Faculté de médecine, other Polytech specialties and the 2025-26 Polytech brochure (PDF not text-extractable; Décathlon/Colas examples unverified). Further departmental instances likely. The WebFetch tool returns model-summarised text, so quotes are as returned; English-language DU quotes originate from an English page, French quotes are original.
